scope: isolated local native services; synthetic data only

findings.check: Auth SMTP restricts fixture recipients and application mail is captured without forwarding
real Supabase Auth migrates its isolated schema and starts
only the eight maintained application migrations apply to the fresh database
real PostgREST and the local TLS API gateway start with separate client and service roles
the unchanged AVES application starts against local-only services
email signup requires confirmation, and SMTP confirmation plus PKCE establish the root account session
Australia, Colombia and New Zealand drafts persist through real user-scoped HTTP and database writes
same-key retries preserve one saved plan and reject changed payloads
a new password session reopens all countries, saves an edit and rejects a stale tab
another account cannot read or edit plans, become an owner or bypass database row permissions
legacy Australian cookies migrate to root without losing the country query or overwriting a newer user
New Zealand quote submission freezes the private brief, notifies once and prevents guest edits
only the owner can draft and issue a proposal, which becomes visible only to its guest
country enquiries save durable receipts, versioned consent and one notification despite retries
legacy Colombian and Australian enquiry URLs store in the same shared backend
notification rejection preserves the stored enquiry and records a distinct failure
password recovery uses a one-time email callback, changes credentials and sign-out revokes refresh
an owned draft deletes through the real API with revision protection

limitations: No browser automation or physical phone run against this local stack
No hosted Google OAuth, provider redirect allowlist or real inbox delivery is verified
Fresh native PostgreSQL/Auth/PostgREST are representative services, not the hosted Supabase configuration
SMTP mail and Resend-compatible responses are captured locally; provider acceptance is simulated
